as_told.title: Air Force closes Project Blue Book

plain: The story is that in 1969 the US Air Force shut down Project Blue Book, its official UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and used a scientific report to justify it. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas says the Air Force wanted to get out of the UFO business and, in closing Blue Book, "even quoted" the Condon report, a study led by a scientist named Edward Condon. The guest Bryce Zabel, speaking in an episode about Hollywood and UFOs, tells it without mentioning Condon. He describes the Air Force as "holding the line" and closing Blue Book in '69 with the attitude "we're washing our hands of that." Salas speaks from his background in the Air Force, while Zabel sums it up as general history without naming a source. Both tell it because it marks the point where the government publicly said it was done with UFOs, which, if the closure was a show, would mean the real study carried on out of sight.
